land.text: the Frankish lands east of the Rhine: Saxony, Austrasia, Alamannia, Bavaria and the March of Carinthia, with Speyer, Worms and Mainz on the left bank (Treaty of Verdun, August 843)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks shape of 849 contains 1,807 of the 1,810 cells of East Francia's first shape. The Carolingian empire (rel-carolingian-empire) is the umbrella over the three Verdun kingdoms.

land.text: East Francia under Conrad I, elected 10 November 911; Lotharingia broke away in November 911 (west-franks dossier)

successors.note: The East Francia page treats the Kingdom of Germany as the same kingdom under a new dynasty (infobox 'Disestablished: 962'); Cliopatria has two rows (East Franks 850-910, Kingdom of Germany 911-961). Colour continuity (family germany) is recommended to the eu-08 dossier.

capitals.name: Regensburg (Ratisbon)
capitals.note: Louis the German page: Bavaria, 'where he made Regensburg the seat of his government'. Arnulf died at Ratisbon on 8 December 899. The court was itinerant: the infobox says 'Various, including Frankfurt and Ratisbon (Regensburg)'.

capitals.name: Frankfurt
capitals.note: Second seat named in the infobox; Louis the German died at his palace in Frankfurt (28 August 876), Charles the Fat held his November 887 assembly there and Louis the Child died there in September 911. Dates of use are not given by the pages.

rulers.name: Louis the German
rulers.note: King list on the East Francia page: Louis the German 843-876; died 28 August 876 (Louis the German page).

rulers.name: Carloman
rulers.title: king in Bavaria (joint heir)
rulers.note: Granted Bavaria in 864 (Louis the German page); stroke in 879 (Charles the Fat page).

rulers.name: Louis the Younger
rulers.title: king in Saxony, Franconia and Thuringia; also Bavaria from 879/880 (joint heir)

rulers.name: Charles the Fat
rulers.title: king in Alamannia from 876; sole king of East Francia from 882
rulers.note: The king list gives 882-887 for his rule of the whole; deposed in November 887.

rulers.name: Arnulf of Carinthia
rulers.note: Elected after Charles the Fat's deposition in November 887; died 8 December 899 (Arnulf page).

rulers.name: Louis the Child
rulers.note: Crowned at Forchheim on 4 February 900 (Louis the Child page: reign begins 899); died 20 or 24 September 911.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins East Francia in 850 but the page puts its birth at the Treaty of Verdun, August 843. The 850 outline stands for 843-849: it lies inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks of 849 and takes in Speyer-Worms-Mainz on the left bank. The East Francia page gives no area, so no infobox comparison was possible.

correction.text: Saxony, Austrasia, Alamannia, Bavaria and the March of Carinthia, with the Speyer-Worms-Mainz district: 'Louis the German ... received the eastern, mostly Germanic-speaking lands' at Verdun

keyframe_review.note: 436,487 km2, 850-859 (the Germany, Austria, Hungary and Slovenia-Croatia cells of Pannonia). The Louis the German page gives Verdun as 'the bulk of the lands lying east of the Rhine' and adds 'Carniola and Lower Pannonia' to his Bavarian realm in 828, which is why the shape reaches the Balaton; the page does not draw a boundary. His invasion of West Francia in 858-859 failed and left no ground (war entry).

435,168 km2, 860-869: the same outline. Louis granted Carloman Bavaria in 864 and divided the rest of his lands among his sons in 865 (Saxony with Franconia and Thuringia to Louis the Younger, Swabia with Raetia to Charles the Fat), sub-kingdoms inside one kingdom, so no border moves.

513,367 km2, 870-874: +337 cells over the 860 shape, the East Frankish share of Lothair II's realm at Meerssen on 8 August 870: most of Lothair's Austrasia with the eastern part 'including both Aachen and Metz', most of Frisia and most of the Upper Burgundy left to Lothair. Cliopatria's West Franks add of 349 cells for the western share does not overlap these 337 cells.
512,735 km2, one year: the 870 outline within 0.1 percent (Cliopatria splits the row for a reason the pages do not give). No event.

430,361 km2, 876-877: Cliopatria takes 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) from the East Franks and gives them to the West Franks. The pages say the opposite: after Louis the German died (28 August 876) Charles the Bald attacked but was beaten at Andernach on 8 October 876, and 'Louis the Younger defeated the much-larger host of West Francia'. The cells stay East Frankish. The west-franks dossier removes the same cells from its 876 shape.

union.text: Cliopatria's 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) that it moves from the East Franks to the West Franks in 876-881

correction.text: East Francia of 876 with the Rhineland, Alsace and Swiss cells that Cliopatria wrongly gives to the West Franks: nothing was lost at Andernach

keyframe_review.note: 430,345 km2, 878-879: still without the 342 cells (see 876). The Ribemont page: November 878 Louis the Younger and Louis the Stammerer agreed at Fourons to respect each other's successors; in 879 Louis the Younger reached Verdun and accepted the western part of Lotharingia. No cell moved before February 880.

union.text: Cliopatria's 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) that it moves from the East Franks to the West Franks in 876-881

correction.text: East Francia of 878 with the 342 cells Cliopatria gives to the West Franks

keyframe_review.note: 484,365 km2, 880-881: right in adding western Lotharingia at Ribemont (February 880: 'the East Frankish king's possession of the whole of Lotharingia, including the western part that West Francia had gained by the Treaty of Meerssen'), but it still lacks the 342 cells (only 1 of them is inside the 880 shape).

union.text: Cliopatria's 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) that it moves from the East Franks to the West Franks in 876-881

correction.text: East Francia after Ribemont: the whole of Lotharingia and the 342 cells

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 882-887, which Cliopatria draws as part of the West Franks (the whole Carolingian empire of Charles the Fat in one shape; see the west-franks dossier). The Charles the Fat page: Louis the Younger died 20 January 882, which left Charles to reunite East Francia, including Saxony and Bavaria; he took the West Frankish crown in 885 (crowned rex in Gallia, 20 May 885 at Grand) without giving up East Francia. The 887 shape stands for these years (it holds Lotharingia and 223 of the 342 cells) PLUS the 117 Transjurane cells: Cliopatria's 887 East Franks drops them because it starts its Upper Burgundy shape in 887, but the Upper Burgundy page dates the kingdom to 888 ('The Kingdom of Upper Burgundy was established in 888 by the Welf king Rudolph I') and has the land 'politically close to East Francia' since Meerssen (870), so the corrected 876-881 keyframes hold it and nothing takes it away before 888 (ledger loss 888, counterpart upper-burgundy). The Wilhelminer War in the March of Pannonia ran 882-884. Corrected after review (eu-07-d): the first version omitted the Transjurane cells.

union.text: Transjurania (Upper Burgundy): the 117 cells of Cliopatria's Upper Burgundy shape of 887 that East Francia held since Meerssen (870)

correction.text: all East Francia under Charles the Fat: Saxony, Bavaria, Alamannia and Lotharingia, with Transjurania (Upper Burgundy) until Rudolph I's election in 888

keyframe_review.note: 556,403 km2, drawn 887-891: right for 888-891 only. Arnulf deposed Charles the Fat in November 887 (the Arnulf page: diet at Tribur; the Charles the Fat page: an assembly at Frankfurt; both: by 17 November 887 Charles was out of power) and received East Francia; the Arnulf page's infobox has him 'King of Lotharingia 887-894' and its lead says 'He also ruled Lotharingia' (the unquoted words 'the only other territory' of the first version are not on the page). Upper Burgundy took the Transjurane cells in 888 (Upper Burgundy page; ledger loss 888), so this shape, which lacks them, holds from 888; the 889-890 recognitions of Louis the Blind and Rudolph took no further land from it.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 888-891 only: Charles the Fat's East Francia under Arnulf without Transjurania, which Rudolph I took in 888; 887 itself is in east-franks_882, which still holds Transjurania

keyframe_review.note: 556,608 km2, drawn 892-895: right for 892-894 only. Arnulf failed to conquer Great Moravia in 892 and 893, 'gained part of its territory, present-day western Hungary' around 893-894 (that land is inside the shape since 850, Transdanubia) and beat the Vikings on the Dyle in September 891. Lotharingia (538 cells) is East Frankish land until Arnulf crowns Zwentibold in May 895; the shape then loses it to the new state (east-franks_895).

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 892-894 only, with Lotharingia as direct East Frankish land; from May 895 see east-franks_895

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 895 only: Arnulf crowns his son Zwentibold king of Lotharingia at the Diet of Worms in May 895. Cliopatria's 892 East Franks shape keeps Lotharingia for 892-895 (538 cells, all inside it) and its Middle Franks shape draws it for 899 only; the 538 cells belong to kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold in the drawing (ledger split and vassal_start 895-5), as East Frankish vassal land, so they are taken out of this shape. Added after review (eu-07-d) to end the double drawing of Lotharingia in 895-900.

correction.text: East Francia without Zwentibold's Lotharingia, which Arnulf made a sub-kingdom in May 895

keyframe_review.note: 730,939 km2, drawn 896-897: +657 cells of northern and central Italy (and Corsica) from Arnulf's second Italian campaign (Pavia, then Rome on 21 February 896, imperial coronation 22 February). The page says that about two weeks later he suffered a stroke and returned to Bavaria, and that after Formosus died Lambert and Berengar 'killed Arnulf's officials, forcing Ratold to flee', so that 'For the rest of his life Arnulf exercised very little control in Italy' (quote corrected by reviewer eu-07-d) in 896. The Italian block is right for 896 only. Corsica is in Cliopatria's block; the page is silent on it. Lotharingia (538 cells, inside the shape as drawn) is taken out: it is Zwentibold's kingdom, East Frankish vassal land (reviewer finding eu-07-d).

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 896 only, without Zwentibold's Lotharingia: Arnulf holds the Italian block from the capture of Rome in February 896 until his officials are killed later that year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 897 only: after Arnulf's control of Italy ended in 896, the 898 shape (without Italy) is right for 897 too.

correction.text: East Francia without the Italian block and without Zwentibold's Lotharingia

keyframe_review.note: 559,419 km2, one year: East Francia with Lotharingia (Zwentibold's sub-kingdom since May 895) and Transdanubia. Adjusted after review (eu-07-d): the 538 Lotharingian cells in the shape are drawn by kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold, so they are subtracted here. No event of its own.

correction.text: East Francia with Transdanubia, without Zwentibold's Lotharingia (a sub-kingdom since May 895)

keyframe_review.note: 434,952 km2, one year: Cliopatria drops Lotharingia from the East Franks and gives it to its Middle Franks row (538 cells, all inside the 898 and 900 shapes). That is what the east-franks dossier needs: the Lotharingia page has Arnulf appoint Zwentibold king of Lotharingia in May 895 and the kingdom 'ruled semi-independently' until Zwentibold was overthrown on 13 August 900. The land is the new state kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold (East Frankish vassal, ledger 895-900), so the shape is right as drawn, without a union (first version unioned Middle Franks 899 into this shape and double-drew it; corrected after review, eu-07-d).

522,040 km2, 900-910: right in taking Lotharingia back after Zwentibold ('Louis succeeded Zwentibold in 900'; Zwentibold killed 13 August 900) and in dropping the Transdanubian and Slavonian cells (180 cells; Cliopatria gives them to the Magyars from 900: the Louis the Child page has Magyars ravaging Bavaria in 900 and defeating the Bavarians at Pressburg in 907, without saying when Pannonia was lost). Years change only: the page ends the Carolingian line in September 911, not 910, so the shape holds 900-911. The 538 Lotharingian cells are inside this shape: East Francia takes Lotharingia back from 900 (ledger gain 900-8, counterpart kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold); the year of an event is the first year of the new shape.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, extended to 911: Louis the Child died on 20 or 24 September 911 and Conrad I was elected on 10 November 911

ledger.note: 843: the Treaty of Verdun gives Louis the German the eastern Frankish lands. 'In August 843, after three years of civil war ... the Treaty of Verdun was signed by his three sons and heirs'; Louis received 'Saxony, Austrasia, Alamannia, Bavaria, and the March of Carinthia' and, on the Louis the German page, 'a district around Speyer, Worms, and Mainz' west of the Rhine and Regensburg as his seat. The pages give no boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 850 outline.

region.text: Saxony, Austrasia, Alamannia, Bavaria and the March of Carinthia, with Speyer, Worms and Mainz

ledger.note: 844: Louis the German subjects the Obotrites. 'In 844, he forced the Obotrites to accept his authority and had their prince, Gozzmovil, put to death.' The page gives no tribute terms; the Obotrites stay a separate state (obotrites dossier).

region.text: the Obotrite lands between the Elbe and the Baltic

ledger.note: 869: Lothair II dies and his uncles quarrel over his realm. He 'died without legitimate children'; Charles the Bald 'had himself crowned at Metz that same year', but Louis the German forced him to partition Lotharingia. The west-franks dossier records the same contest.

region.text: Lothair II's whole realm (Cliopatria draws it as 'Lower Burgundy' 866-869)

ledger.note: 870: Meerssen ends the contest for Lotharingia, 8 August. 'The treaty was concluded on 8 August 870 at Meerssen.'

870: Meerssen gives Louis the German the east of Lothair II's realm. He received most of Lothair's Austrasia with the eastern part 'including both Aachen and Metz', most of Frisia and most of the Upper Burgundy left to Lothair; Hugh, Lothair's illegitimate son, kept the Duchy of Alsace. Louis joined the new land to his son Louis the Younger's sub-kingdom. The region is Cliopatria's 337-cell addition; the page names no boundary beyond Aachen and Metz.

region.text: eastern Austrasia with Aachen and Metz, most of Frisia and most of Upper Burgundy

ledger.note: 876: Charles the Bald invades East Francia after Louis the German's death (28 August). The Louis the Younger page has the brothers succeeding 'in accordance with the prearranged partition'; Charles's attack on eastern Lotharingia is on the Treaty of Meerssen page. Cliopatria shows the invaded cells as West Frankish in 876-881; the pages show no ground kept.

region.text: Cliopatria's 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) that it moves from the East Franks to the West Franks in 876-881

ledger.note: 876: 8 October, Louis the Younger beats the West Franks at Andernach. At Andernach, Louis 'defeated the much-larger host of West Francia'; the cells stay East Frankish.

region.text: Cliopatria's 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) that it moves from the East Franks to the West Franks in 876-881

ledger.note: 880: Ribemont gives western Lotharingia to East Francia. 'In February 880, at Ribemont ... It confirmed the East Frankish king's possession of the whole of Lotharingia, including the western part that West Francia had gained by the Treaty of Meerssen (870).' In 879 Louis the Younger had reached Verdun and accepted the offer of the western part. The region is Cliopatria's 880 addition (248 cells); the page names no town.

region.text: the western part of Lotharingia that West Francia held from 870

ledger.note: 884: Svatopluk of Great Moravia swears fidelity to Charles the Fat. 'In 884, at Kaumberg, Svatopluk I of Great Moravia swore an oath of fidelity to Charles', giving him 'new Slavic allies'; the page does not call Moravia a tributary and gives no terms.

region.text: Transjurania, Rudolph I elected and crowned at St. Maurice

ledger.note: 888: the Transjurane magnates elect Rudolph I and Upper Burgundy leaves East Francia. 'The nobles and leading clergy of Upper Burgundy assembled at the Abbey of St. Maurice, Agaunum' and 'The Kingdom of Upper Burgundy was established in 888 by the Welf king Rudolph I' (Upper Burgundy page); Meerssen (870) had made Upper Burgundy 'politically close to East Francia'. The page gives no month. The region is the 117 cells of Cliopatria's Upper Burgundy shape of 887 that lie inside East Francia's 870 shape (the Meerssen gain, ledger 870-8). Mirrors upper-burgundy's 888 found event. Added after review (eu-07-d).

888: Rudolph I claims Lotharingia. 'Apparently on the basis of this election, Rudolph claimed the whole of Lotharingia, taking much of modern Lorraine and Alsace.' Mirrors the upper-burgundy contest_start (same zone and year); the page gives no month. Added after review (eu-07-d).

892, July: the oath of 884 is broken and Arnulf invades Moravia. 'Svatopluk, however, broke his pledges, so Arnulf decided to invade Moravia in 891'; 'Arnulf's invasion started in July 892, but he failed to defeat Svatopluk'; 'The war against Moravia seems to have continued until 894' (Svatopluk I page; it dates the decision to 891 and the campaign to 892). Year and month are the invasion's. The Arnulf page has Arnulf failing 'to conquer Great Moravia in campaigns in 892, 893 and 899'. Raised from confidence 1 after review (eu-07-d).

894: the fighting between Rudolph and Arnulf ends. Arnulf 'rapidly forced Rudolph to abandon Lotharingia in return for recognition as king of Upper Burgundy'; 'hostilities between Rudolph and Arnulf seem to have continued intermittently until 894' (Rudolph I page, no month). Mirrors upper-burgundy's contest_end 894. Added after review (eu-07-d).

894: Arnulf takes Lombardy. In January 894 'Bergamo fell during Arnulf's first Italian campaign. He took Milan, drove Guy from Pavia, and was proclaimed King of Italy'; fever stopped him late in 894. Region: Lombardy as my reading of Bergamo, Milan and Pavia.

895: Bohemia leaves Great Moravia for Arnulf. 'In 895, the Duchy of Bohemia broke away from Great Moravia and became Arnulf's vassal state' (Arnulf page); the Duchy of Bohemia page: Spytihnev 'swore allegiance to the East Frankish king Arnulf of Carinthia in Regensburg'. The first version named Borivoj I, which neither page says.

895, May: Arnulf cuts Lotharingia out of East Francia as a kingdom for his son Zwentibold. The Diet of Worms, May 895: 'At the same assembly he crowned his illegitimate son Zwentibold as the king of Lotharingia' (Arnulf page). The 538 cells leave the East Frankish keyframes (east-franks_895) and are drawn by kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold, still as East Frankish vassal land (next event). Added after review (eu-07-d).

895, May: Lotharingia becomes a sub-kingdom under the East Frankish crown. At the Diet of Worms in May 895 Arnulf 'crowned his illegitimate son Zwentibold as the king of Lotharingia' (Arnulf page); the Lotharingia page: he 'ruled semi-independently until he was overthrown and killed by Reginar on August 13, 900'. Drawn as vassal land (lighter tint); the cells belong to kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold, not to the East Frankish keyframes.

896: Arnulf takes Rome and is crowned emperor. Arnulf took Rome by force on 21 February 896, freeing Pope Formosus, and Formosus crowned him emperor at St. Peter's on 22 February. The region is Cliopatria's 896 Italian block (657 cells, northern and central Italy and Corsica), which is wider than the places the page names (Pavia, Milan, Rome).

region.text: the Italian block of Cliopatria's 896 shape

ledger.note: 896, from April: Arnulf's Italy slips away. After the coronation 'Arnulf had a stroke, forcing him to call off the campaign and return to Bavaria'; 'That same year Pope Formosus died, leaving Lambert once again in power', and Lambert and Berengar killed 'any officials who had been appointed by Arnulf', 'forcing Ratold to flee from Milan to Bavaria'; 'For the rest of his life Arnulf exercised very little control in Italy'. Month 4 is the earliest the pages allow ('On 4 April 896, Formosus died', Pope Formosus page; set by reviewer eu-07-d so the loss follows the February gain). Cliopatria keeps the block to 897.

896, from April: the fighting for Italy ends in Berengar's and Lambert's favour after Formosus's death (4 April 896): 'For the rest of his life Arnulf exercised very little control in Italy' (no further campaign on the page). Month as for the loss (reviewer eu-07-d).

900: the Hungarians occupy Pannonia. The page says they 'attacked and occupied Pannonia' in 900 (the land west of the Danube), on the way back from Italy after Arnulf's death at the end of 899, and that Arnulf's death released them from their alliance with East Francia; it gives no month. The region is Cliopatria's 180 cells (Transdanubia and eastern Slavonia). The counterpart stays principality-of-hungary: the gazetteer gives 177 of the 180 cells to Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary shape of 900 and none to its Magyars row (the reviewer suspected the Magyars row). Second page: Louis the Child ('In 900, during the Hungarian invasions of Europe, the Magyar army ravaged Bavaria'). Raised from confidence 1 after review (eu-07-d).

region.text: Transdanubia and eastern Slavonia, the March of Pannonia

ledger.note: 900, 13 August: Zwentibold is overthrown and killed. He 'ruled semi-independently until he was overthrown and killed by Reginar on August 13, 900. The kingdom then ceased to exist and became a duchy' (Lotharingia page). The Louis the Child page: 'Louis succeeded Zwentibold in 900', so Lotharingia becomes direct land of the crown.
900: Lotharingia returns to Louis the Child on Zwentibold's death (13 August); in 903 he appointed Gebhard duke ('duke of the kingdom that many call Lothair's').

911: the dossier ends and with it the bridging end of the Obotrite tribute (844). The pages date no end of the Obotrites' submission to East Francia; Hermann Billung's march of 936 (Billung March page) shows the Saxon kings still ruling them.

911: the dossier ends and with it the bridging end of Bohemia's vassalage (895). The pages say nothing of Bohemia after 895; the Kingdom of Germany dossier should say whether Bohemia stayed a vassal. Duchy of Bohemia page (follow-up after review, eu-07-d): the principality 'existed as independent state though still in the shadow of East Francia'; the page does not call Bohemia a vassal after Spytihnev's oath of 895, says nothing of 911, and has Wenceslaus 'submitting to King Henry in 929'. The end stays a drawing end (confidence 1).

911: the Carolingian line of East Francia ends and the kingdom passes to Conrad I. 'Louis died at Frankfurt am Main on 20 or 24 September 911'; the East Francia page: 'Duke Conrad I, then the Duke of Franconia, was elected to replace him on 10 November.' Saxon, Franconian, Bavarian and Swabian nobles chose a new king; Lotharingia went to Charles the Simple (west-franks dossier). The page treats East Francia as continuing as the Kingdom of Germany.

region.text: the whole kingdom of Louis the Child

wars.name: Louis the German's invasion of West Francia
wars.outcome: Louis invaded in 858 and issued a charter dated the first year of his reign in West Francia; the campaign failed through desertion and the loyalty of the Aquitanian bishops, and the brothers swore peace at Koblenz on 7 June 860. No border moved.
wars.note: The infobox gives his West Frankish reign as 858-859 (a few months).

wars.name: Contest for Lothair II's kingdom
wars.outcome: Treaty of Meerssen, 8 August 870: Louis the German takes the east of Lotharingia (Aachen, Metz, most of Frisia, most of Upper Burgundy); Charles the Bald the west and Lower Burgundy.
wars.note: Lothair II's Italian brother Louis II, the heir, was 'campaigning against the Emirate of Bari'.

wars.name: Charles the Bald's invasion of East Francia

zones.text: Cliopatria's 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) that it moves from the East Franks to the West Franks in 876-881

wars.outcome: Charles was beaten by Louis the Younger at Andernach on 8 October 876; no ground was kept.
wars.note: Cliopatria draws the invaded cells as West Frankish for 876-881; keyframes east-franks_876/878/880 correct that.

wars.name: Louis the Younger's West Frankish succession bid and the Treaty of Ribemont
wars.outcome: Fourons (November 878), the invasion as far as Verdun (879) and Ribemont (February 880): East Francia keeps the whole of Lotharingia; the West Frankish border set then 'stayed largely the same until the Late Middle Ages'.
wars.note: The Ribemont page does not mention Andernach; the Louis the Younger page does.

wars.name: Wilhelminer War
wars.outcome: A war in the March of Pannonia, 'ran from 882 to 884' (Charles the Fat page); the page gives no result and no border moved.
wars.note: Opened only for the date; the war's cause and outcome are not on the page.

wars.name: Arnulf's war with Rudolph I of Upper Burgundy
wars.outcome: Rudolph claimed the whole of Lotharingia after his election in 888 and took much of modern Lorraine and Alsace; Arnulf 'rapidly forced Rudolph to abandon Lotharingia in return for recognition as king of Upper Burgundy'; hostilities 'seem to have continued intermittently until 894'. East Francia keeps Lotharingia; the Transjurane cells left it by Rudolph's election (ledger loss 888), not by war.
wars.note: The page dates neither the forcing nor the recognition; Arnulf's acknowledgement of Rudolph's rule is also on the Upper Burgundy page. Added after review (eu-07-d).

wars.name: Arnulf's Moravian campaigns
wars.outcome: Arnulf failed to conquer Great Moravia in 892, 893 and 899; he gained part of its land around 893-894 (western Hungary, already inside the shape); in 899 'he used Magyar help to impose some control over Moravia'.
wars.note: Bohemia broke away from Moravia in 895 and became Arnulf's vassal.

wars.name: Arnulf's Italian campaigns
wars.outcome: January 894 Bergamo, Milan and Pavia taken; October 1895 second campaign; Rome on 21 February 896 and imperial coronation on 22 February; a stroke and Lambert's and Berengar's counter-moves ended Arnulf's control in 896.
wars.note: Guy of Spoleto died late in 894.

wars.name: Magyar invasions of East Francia
wars.outcome: Magyars ravaged Bavaria in 900 and Saxony twice in 906; in 907 they defeated the Bavarians at Pressburg (killing Margrave Luitpold) and in 910 beat Louis the Child's army at Augsburg.
wars.note: The page does not date the loss of the Pannonian march.

certainty.note: The Verdun lines in the west are described by rivers and regions, not surveyed; the eastern marches (Carinthia, Pannonia, the Slav frontier on the Elbe) are soft throughout.

The frontier with West Francia is treaty-fixed from Meerssen (870, 'the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saone and Rhone', west-franks dossier) and Ribemont (880) and is the sharp exception; the Slav, Moravian, Bohemian and Magyar frontiers stay soft, and the 896 Italian block is a campaign, not a border.

sources.title: East Francia

sources.title: Treaty of Meerssen

sources.title: Louis the German

sources.title: Treaty of Ribemont

sources.title: Arnulf of Carinthia
sources.note: Election 887, Moravia 892-899, Italy 894-896, Zwentibold 895, Bohemia 895, death 8 December 899.

sources.title: Lotharingia
sources.note: Zwentibold's kingdom 895-13 August 900; the 870 and 880 treaties; 911 and 925.

sources.title: Louis the Younger

sources.title: Louis the Child

sources.title: Upper Burgundy
sources.note: Follow-up after review: 888 election of Rudolph I at St. Maurice, the kingdom established in 888, 'politically close to East Francia' since Meerssen (ledger loss 888).

sources.title: Rudolph I of Burgundy
sources.note: Follow-up after review: Rudolph's claim to Lotharingia after 888, Arnulf's pressure, hostilities until 894 (contest 888-894).

sources.title: Svatopluk I of Moravia
sources.note: Follow-up after review: Svatopluk broke his pledges, Arnulf's invasion July 892, war until 894 (vassal_end Great Moravia).

sources.title: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin
sources.note: Follow-up after review: Hungarians occupy Pannonia in 900 after Arnulf's death (loss 900).

sources.title: Duchy of Bohemia
sources.note: Follow-up after review: Spytihnev's oath to Arnulf at Regensburg (895); 'independent state though still in the shadow of East Francia'; Wenceslaus submits to Henry in 929.

notes: East Francia (eu-07-d). First pass: nine pages, the whole budget (East Francia, Treaty of Meerssen, Louis the German, Treaty of Ribemont, Charles the Fat, Arnulf of Carinthia, Lotharingia, Louis the Younger, Louis the Child). Repair after the review: five more pages opened for the reviewer's findings (Upper Burgundy, Rudolph I of Burgundy, Svatopluk I of Moravia, Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin, Duchy of Bohemia), over the budget. None of the pages gives an area, so no infobox comparison was possible. Cliopatria rows. (1) 876-881: Cliopatria moves 342 cells (Alsace, the Rhineland, Swiss lands) from the East Franks to the West Franks (876) and back only in part; the pages show Andernach keeping them. Verdicts adjust for 876, 878 and 880, mirroring the west-franks dossier. (2) 882-886 are missing: Cliopatria draws Charles the Fat's whole empire as West Franks; new keyframe east-franks_882 (882-887) = the 887 shape PLUS the 117 Transjurane cells (Upper Burgundy 887 inside East Franks 870) that Cliopatria's East Franks 887 drops although no page has them leave before Rudolph I's election in 888 (ledger loss 888, counterpart upper-burgundy); east-franks_887 holds 888-891. (3) 896-897 Italy: the page ends Arnulf's control in 896; keyframes 896 (adjust) and 897 (new). (4) 895-900 Lotharingia, decided with middle-franks after the review: Cliopatria draws Zwentibold's Lotharingia as East Franks land in 892-898 and as a Middle Franks shape in 899. It is now a separate state, kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold (split from Cliopatria's Middle Franks row, written in this batch), East Frankish vassal land from May 895 to 13 August 900. The east-franks keyframes subtract Middle Franks 899 (new east-franks_895; 896, 897 and 898 adjusted; 899 ok as drawn), the ledger has a split and a vassal_start in May 895 and the vassal_end and gain in August 900, and east-franks_900 takes the land back. Year convention: the year of an event is the first year of the new shape, so the new dossier's keyframes stop in 899. The alternative (Lotharingia as direct East Frankish land, no sub-kingdom) is described in that dossier's notes. (5) 900-910: the Pannonia loss is now dated by the Hungarian conquest page (occupied in 900, confidence 2). Disagreement with the reviewer: the counterpart stays principality-of-hungary, not magyars, because the gazetteer gives 177 of the 180 cells to Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary shape of 900 and none to its Magyars row. (6) The end is September 911 on the pages (Conrad I elected 10 November 911); Cliopatria ends the row in 910 and starts the Kingdom of Germany in 911, so 911 is drawn twice unless the Kingdom of Germany dossier starts in November. Not settled. (7) Upper Burgundy: loss 888 (Transjurania) and contest 888-894 over Lorraine and Alsace added as mirrors of the upper-burgundy events; the Rudolph I page has hostilities 'intermittently until 894'. Thin items worked: the 892 vassal_end of Great Moravia is dated by the Svatopluk I page (invasion July 892; confidence 2); the 911 vassal_end events for the Obotrites and Bohemia stay drawing ends at confidence 1 (the Duchy of Bohemia page calls Bohemia 'independent state though still in the shadow of East Francia', not a vassal, and dates its submission to Henry to 929); the 895 Bohemia quote was corrected (the first version named Borivoj I; the Duchy of Bohemia page has Spytihnev swearing allegiance at Regensburg). Quotes corrected: 'the only other territory' (Arnulf page) is not on the page; the Arnulf infobox has 'King of Lotharingia 887-894'. The Cliopatria relation '(Allegiance of East Franks to Carolingian Empire)' 850-881 and 887-921 is not supported by any page opened (the East Francia page calls the kingdom independent after Verdun); no vassal events were recorded for it. The Charles the Fat page puts the deposition at an assembly in Frankfurt, the Arnulf page at Tribur (November 887); the East Francia text says 888 where its king list says 887. Counterparts without a dossier: kingdom-of-lotharingia (Lothair II, 855-869; eu-07-x or a gap-filler). The vassal counterparts great-moravia, duchy-of-bohemia, obotrites and principality-of-hungary have dossiers elsewhere or in this batch. Gazetteer: all names used resolve (Lombardy, Lorraine, Alsace; Cliopatria shapes).
